AfterCardChangedPiles.issue: Rollup of guard G1 per binding rule 4. The core is right -- the deck-pile filter, the anti-recursion skip set, and the bottom-of-deck placement all match -- but C#'s `clonedBy == null` clause has no sim counterpart.

guards.what: G1 (DORMANT): C# refuses to clone a card that some other model put in the deck (`clonedBy == null`, BingBong.cs:25); the sim's after_card_added_to_deck receives no such argument and clones everything
guards.issue: MECHANISM: CardPileCmd.Add takes a `clonedBy` AbstractModel and BingBong passes `this` when adding its own clone (BingBong.cs:30), so C# has TWO independent anti-recursion defences -- the CardsToSkip set AND the clonedBy argument. The clonedBy clause is broader than recursion, though: it suppresses cloning for ANY model-added card, not just Bing Bong's own. The sim's hook signature is `after_card_added_to_deck(self, run, card)` (relics/base.py:208) with no adder argument, so the port can only reproduce the CardsToSkip half (bing_bong.py:34-36) and will clone a card another relic added where C# would not. REACHABILITY (DORMANT): it needs a second ported model that adds a deck card WITH a clonedBy argument. The sim's only other deck-add interceptor is the egg family's modify_card_being_added_to_deck (relics/_eggs.py), which SUBSTITUTES a card rather than adding one, so no ported path sets clonedBy today. Porting Dolly's Mirror (currently a behaviourless stub -- see the sweep findings) or any other card-duplicating relic makes it live, and in the runaway direction: two cloners would feed each other.

guards.what: N1: CardPilePosition.Bottom (BingBong.cs:30) vs the sim's run.add_card append (run.py:544)
guards.rationale: The game's CardPile indexes 0 = top, so Bottom is the end of the list, and RunState.add_card appends. Same placement. This matters for the same reason run.transform_card's docstring (run.py:419-427) gives for its own end-placement: the combat-start UnstableShuffle is order-dependent, so a top-vs-bottom slip would desync every subsequent draw.

guards.what: N2: the sim keys its skip set on `id(card)` (bing_bong.py:34-38) where C# uses a HashSet<CardModel> of references
guards.rationale: CPython reuses id() values after an object is collected, so an id-keyed set is in principle stale-prone. It is safe here because the only id ever inserted belongs to the clone, and the clone is appended to run.deck on the very next line -- it is reachable for the rest of the run, so its id cannot be reissued while the entry is live. The entry is also consumed on first match (line 35), exactly like C#'s HashSet.Remove-in-the-condition. Recorded because the safety depends on the add_card call that follows, not on the set itself: a future edit that clones without adding would introduce a genuine aliasing bug.

guards.what: N3: Flash() and the deck-add preview (BingBong.cs:27, 30)
guards.rationale: RelicModel.Flash() / base.Status / ShowCounter / DisplayAmount / CanonicalVars / ExtraHoverTips / Cmd.Wait / CardCmd.Preview are presentation only -- the relic bar's glow, counter and hover text, and animation timing. The sim has no relic UI. Waived under the shared contract's presentation/animation exclusion, not under an unreachability claim.
